records.title: Register for School
records.summary: Register online, with the board's fillable form, or at your home school. You need proof of your child's age and proof of a Niagara address; an up-to-date immunization record must be on file with the public health unit. Families whose children were born outside Canada start with the DSBN Welcome Centre.

records.title: School Locator
records.summary: The board's own lookup: enter an address to see its area school and the school's mapped boundary (choose the school year first). The board says its maps show general layout only; its planning department answers boundary questions.

records.title: French Immersion
records.summary: DSBN has one entry point: French Immersion starts in Grade 1, with no French needed beforehand. Families register during a yearly window; when we checked, the board had not yet posted the dates or information sessions for the next intake. Transportation follows the same rules as for every DSBN student.

records.title: Secondary programs
records.summary: French Immersion continues in Grades 9 to 12 at five DSBN high schools (listed on the board's French Immersion schools page). Core French is offered at every DSBN high school.

records.title: Attending a school outside your area
records.summary: We could not find a published DSBN procedure for asking to attend a school other than your area school. Ask the school's principal, or the board's planning department, how requests are handled and when to apply. Bus service to a school other than your home school is only provided for approved system-wide programs (see transportation).

records.title: Transportation Eligibility and Service (board policy)
records.summary: Students who live at least 0.8 km (kindergarten), 1.6 km (Grades 1 to 8) or 3.2 km (Grades 9 to 12) from their home school, by the shortest walking route, may get transportation. Students attending a school other than their home school get it only for approved system-wide programs. Niagara Student Transportation Services runs the buses for DSBN and Niagara Catholic.

related.title: Check transportation eligibility for an address (NSTS)

records.title: Special Education
records.summary: The board's special education page, with its special education report (the board's plan for programs and services) and a guide for parents. Start with your child's teacher and principal; they arrange assessments, Individual Education Plans (IEPs) and Identification, Placement and Review Committee (IPRC) meetings.

records.title: Special Education Advisory Committee (SEAC)
records.summary: SEAC meets monthly in public and advises the board on special education programs and services. Its members include representatives of local community associations.

records.title: Multi-Year Accessibility Plan 2023-2028 (PDF)
records.summary: The board's accessibility plan under Ontario's accessibility law. It describes board-wide plans, not the features of a particular school building; ask the school about specific needs.

records.title: DSBN Welcome Centre
records.summary: Registration, settlement and language support for families new to Canada. English as a Second Language support is described on the board's ESL page.

related.title: ESL: English as a Second Language

records.title: Long Term Accommodation Plan 2023-2032 (PDF)
records.summary: The board's plan for school space: each school's capacity, enrolment and projections, and recommended projects by planning area. Recommendations are not decisions. The plan notes that the province's 2017 moratorium on school closures stops accommodation reviews until it is lifted.

related.title: Accommodation Review policy (marked under review because of the 2017 moratorium)

records.title: Student Achievement Plan
records.summary: The board's plan under Ontario's student achievement framework: literacy (EQAO reading and writing, the OSSLT), graduation and credits, and engagement and well-being (suspensions). It reports board results next to Ontario's; it does not set numeric targets. These are board-wide figures, not this school's.

records.title: Parent Involvement Committee (PIC)
records.summary: A parent committee that advises the board. Meetings are public and listed on the page.

records.title: School councils
records.summary: Every school has a parent-led school council; ask the school how to join.

records.title: Board of Trustees
records.summary: Your elected trustees, by area, and how to reach them. Board and committee meetings are public.

records.title: Contact us
records.summary: Start with your child's teacher, then the principal; if that doesn't settle it, contact the school's superintendent. The board's complaints policy sets out the steps.

records.title: Long Term Accommodation Plan 2023-2032, Elementary Planning Area 13 (PDF)

facts.capacity_definition: On-the-ground (OTG) capacity: the provincially recognized pupil space of the building, not counting portables

records.summary: The board's 2023 plan lists this school as Grades 1 to 8 French Immersion with an on-the-ground capacity of 322 and 495 students in 2022, and says it is over capacity and expected to stay over capacity long term. It lists no upcoming project for this planning area. Projections are the board's forecasts, and capacity is building space, not open seats in a grade or program.
